title: Lattice Commerce - credits to inference pathfinding

Discussed free credits, sandbox, VPC requirements, SOC2 and KMS, perf expectations and next steps for pilot and security docs.

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-08-05
- Time: 14:00 PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lina (CSM); Jordan (Lattice), Priya (Lattice), Alex (Lattice)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on PLG onboarding and TTFT for ecommerce personalization. Customer cares about data residency, PII, cost per inference, and predictable latency.

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): hey everybody thanks for joining uh appreciate you making time today hows the afternoon on your side
00:07 Jordan (Lattice): hey Maya yeah good thanks we're in the middle of a release week so appreciate it, short on time but excited to chat
00:13 Maya: perfect we'll keep tight agenda — quick intro, your current stack and constraints, TTFT needs, hosted/dedicated/private fit, next steps. Ethan from SE will chime on benchmarks and pilot plan.
00:27 Ethan (Redwood SE): hi all quick wave, i'll try not to nerd out too early but will cover perf and networking ask at the end
00:34 Alex (Lattice PM): great thanks, quick context from our side: we're a mid-enterprise e-commerce company, about 120 engineers, product teams are running experimentation on personalized recommendations and on-site messaging. We're interested in an LLM for product descriptions and merch suggestions — but PII concerns because we sometimes include order context in prompts.
00:52 Priya (Infra): yeah we own infra and security, our list of must-haves: SOC2 or equivalent, SSO/SAML, support for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) if private, and VPC peering or egress control for hosted. Also latency targets — <200ms tail for simple prompt completions ideally.
01:10 Maya: cool, that's helpful. On SOC2 we provide audit docs and compliance pack — we'll share. For SSO we support SAML/Okta, and for keys we support KMS integrations on Private; Dedicated has options for key controls too. For hosted, we have encryption at-rest and in-transit and configurable retention.
01:32 Jordan: that's good to hear. A key question is TTFT — we want devs to get to first inference quickly via PLG — free credits, quickstart, SDKs. How long does it take typically to go from signup to a first call?
01:45 Lina (CSM): typical PLG path is minutes to first call if you use the SDK and the hosted API — that's what many startups get. For teams with stricter networking we do a guided onboarding and can provision sandbox creds; TTFT for that route is usually 1-3 days.
02:02 Priya: ok so sandbox creds — does that route require inbound peering or can you lock egress? we prefer no inbound and only egress to allowed endpoints.
02:12 Ethan: you can keep traffic outbound from your VPC to Redwood endpoints, we also support VPC connectors for Private where traffic never leaves your VPC. For Dedicated we can place on customer's cloud project with restricted egress. There was a small hiccup earlier where some customers confuse KV cache with K V cache in our docs — apologies if that shows up — but key point: we support prefix caching to reduce cost.
02:36 Jordan: hah yeah saw that in one doc. On the dev experience side, do you have client libs and quickstart templates for Node and Python? Our frontend folks want an example for streaming completions.
02:46 Maya: yep we have SDKs, sample apps, and a streaming example for webhooks/WS. We'll drop a link in the follow-up. Quickstarts include a 200 token demo that runs in <100ms avg depending on model.
03:00 Alex: nice. On pricing and credits — we have a small team budget for a POC. We like free credits to validate end-to-end. Does Redwood offer them and any guardrails?
03:12 Maya: we do offer PLG credits for trial accounts. They can be restricted to certain models and rate limits, and we can set per-token caps. For pilots we often provide a dedicated credit pool and can timebox it.
03:25 Jordan: perfect. Now on choosing hosted vs dedicated vs private: our immediate goal is fast iteration via hosted with credits, but mid-term we may need dedicated for predictable latency and private for the biggest customers with PII/legal constraints. What's typical migration path?
03:43 Ethan: typical flow: hosted for fast prototyping and TTFT; move to Dedicated when you need predictable throughput and isolation; Private if you need full control over networking and KMS/HSM. We support model version pinning so your API calls remain stable across migration.
04:00 Priya: curious about latencies on Dedicated vs Hosted — do you publish benchmarks for p99 under load? We have bursty traffic on Black Friday windows.
04:12 Ethan: we publish performance profiles per model and hardware. For example, medium-sized models at 1k tokens on A100-backed dedicated pools show p50 ~30ms per token and p99 in the few hundreds depending on batching. For burst handling — autoscaling with warm pools reduces cold-starts; we can show historical traces. We'll need realistic sample payloads to run a bench for you.
04:35 Jordan: we can share sample traffic pattern and payload size — mostly short prompts with some convo context up to 512 tokens for personalization.
04:45 Priya: on compliance again — does Redwood provide audit logs for inference requests per user? We need per-request metadata retained for 90 days for our audits.
04:56 Maya: yes audit logs available, retention configurable depending on plan, and for Private you can ship logs to your SIEM. There's an option to redact or not store prompt content at rest if you need that.
05:10 Alex: excellent. Any gotchas for embedding usage? Thinking about vector store integration and cost per embed.
05:18 Ethan: embeddings are straightforward; recommend batching and caching. Quantization choices can affect embed latency; watch for float16 vs int8 differences. Also vendor/competitor note — customers sometimes compare odd latencies to OpenAI/Anthropic models — we try to present apples-to-apples with identical sequence lengths and batching.
05:38 Jordan: okay. Real question on TTFT: can an engineer sign up and call API from dev machine in under 15 minutes?
05:45 Lina: yes for hosted — signup, get creds, call with SDK example — many report <15 minutes. If they want to test within corp network with egress locks may take a day.
05:55 Priya: do you have a hosted IP allowlist? we prefer outbound only but we need to allow certain endpoints through firewall.
06:02 Ethan: we have static IP ranges per region and a list we share with customers; we can also support custom peering for Dedicated or Private which removes the need to open outbound to wide ranges.
06:15 Jordan: Great. Let's talk success criteria for a pilot/proof of concept: what should we measure?
06:22 Maya: typical success metrics: TTFT (time for dev to first call), request latency p50/p95/p99, cost per inference/opportunity (tokens per session), quality metrics (human eval on X prompts), and stability (error rates under load).
06:35 Alex: for us pilot would be 2 weeks, 3 product engineers, ~10k requests/day. If we can validate latency and quality and stay within credit budget we'd consider expanding.
06:47 Ethan: sounds reasonable. For benchmarking we'll recommend a 2-week pilot with a small canary on hosted; we can run identical workloads on Dedicated if you want cost/latency comparisons.
06:58 Priya: if we do canary on hosted, what about data retention and prompt redaction — we must prevent order PII from being stored in logs by default.
07:08 Maya: we can configure redaction off by default, or ship logs to your SIEM for Private. We'll include the configuration options in the security doc.
07:20 Jordan: moving to practicals — can you send the sandbox creds and a quickstart link now or after the call?
07:25 Maya: we'll send creds in follow-up email; for security we'll gate sensitive sandbox for a short approval but standard test account is immediate.
07:33 Alex: thanks. Any immediate blockers from Redwood side for the TTFT path?
07:37 Ethan: none technically — we just need payload samples and a list of models you'd like to evaluate. Also a nod on expected traffic so we can size the trial.
07:47 Priya: i'll share network diagram and the list of blocked outbound ports plus our compliance Qs. Also curious on SSO integration time — how long for SAML SSO with Okta?
07:58 Maya: usually 1-3 business days to set up and test SSO depending on your Okta admin availability. For early pilots often teams use API keys and then move to SSO before broader rollout.
08:10 Jordan: any price ballpark we should expect for Dedicated reservation?
08:15 Maya: rough ballpark depends on model class and committed QPS. We'll send a pricing matrix: hourly reserved pool pricing and example cost per million tokens.
08:24 Alex: perfect. Quick question from me — are there rate limits on free credits? We want to simulate production load during the pilot.
08:31 Lina: credits can be configured for rate limits; for pilots we often lift strict throttles so you can validate under load with a defined cap. We'll coordinate test windows with infra.
08:42 Jordan: ok great. Anything about vendor lock-in? We want portability — can you export model outputs and logs easily?
08:49 Ethan: yes you can export logs and store them wherever; model artifacts are open model-based in many cases — migration guidance available. We'll share an export checklist.
08:59 Priya: nice. One more technical — what's the expected cold-start behavior on Dedicated when scaling up for bursts?
09:07 Ethan: Dedicated uses warm pools and we can configure pre-warming thresholds; cold-starts are possible but you can tune autoscale policies to keep a minimum baseline.
09:15 Jordan: last quickie about evaluation: does Redwood provide eval suites or can we bring our own prompts?
09:22 Maya: both — we have eval harnesses and you can upload your prompt sets; we can tie quality regressions to alerts.
09:30 Alex: ok perfect. That was a lot — super helpful.
09:34 Maya: recap next steps: i'll send pricing + hosted vs dedicated one-pager and quickstart links; Ethan will draft pilot benchmark script; Priya will share network/compliance docs; we'll schedule a 60-min tech deep dive for the week of Aug 18. Anything else?
09:50 Jordan: please include security pack and SOC2 attestation in the email.
09:54 Lina: will do.
09:56 Maya: cool thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the notes and artifacts.
10:00 (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains a few minor mis-hearings; speakers occasionally overlap and some tech terms spelled out (e.g., KMS spelled K M S) — preserved to reflect raw transcript.
